title: Dispatch: xwau type printed activation costs for item operations and state-machine transitions, per-clause readiness (attempt 1, Sonnet)
description:
Implements eshyra-xwau. Read `bd show eshyra-xwau`, `bd show eshyra-olc5.9` (with its notes, in particular the cloud-review S1 closure: faithful-or-absent, the PRINTED_CASTING_TIME_OVERRIDES set, exact-phrase evidence), docs/rules-pack-compiler.md, docs/importer-fix-protocol.md (MANDATORY: this task touches the importer and the generated pack), and ADR 0017/0020. The bd memory magic-item-faithful-or-absent governs: a typed field must be source-faithful, or absent. Locate code by symbol name.

CONTEXT: olc5.9 makes use_item spend the printed turn resource (action / bonus action / reaction) for operations[] that carry a typed activation.cost. Four F2 hook groups stay unlanded: 'action-economy activation' (144 clauses), 'activation action economy' (89), 'reaction and action economy' (7), 'item activation and action-budget ownership' (4). By representation block they break down as: about 150 effects clauses, 72 operations clauses, 17 stateMachine clauses, 3 interItem, 1 containment. Nearly all of them also carry OTHER unlanded hooks.

DESIGN (decided; do not substitute another):
1. TYPE WHAT THE SOURCE PRINTS, NOTHING ELSE. For every magic-item OPERATION and every STATE-MACHINE activate/deactivate TRANSITION that has no typed activation cost today: add a typed cost, using the same shape and the same exact-phrase evidence discipline as olc5.9, ONLY where the item's own SRD text prints the activation action type for that exact operation or transition. Examples: "As a bonus action, you can click the boots' heels together"; "you can use an action to"; "as a reaction when". If the text prints no action type, the cost stays absent (DM-adjudicated). Do not infer it from analogy, item category or the core rules. A narrow exception is allowed only when an SRD core rule names the activity exactly and is cited. For example: drinking a potion or administering one to another creature takes an action (SRD 'Potions' / Use an Object). If you apply that rule to consume/drink operations, cite the exact SRD rule text in the evidence ledger. Otherwise leave them absent and record why.
   Implement this in the importer and curation stage that owns these fields, per the compiler architecture. Do NOT hand-edit generated pack files. Regenerate and keep `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` exact.
2. RUNTIME. use_item already spends a typed operations[] cost (olc5.9). Make a state-machine transition invoked through use_item (activate/deactivate) spend its typed transition cost through the SAME spend path. It refuses when the resource is unavailable in combat and spends nothing out of combat, matching olc5.9 semantics exactly. Fail closed on an unrecognized cost value.
3. READINESS: NO GLOBAL HOOK LANDING. Do NOT add these four hooks to LANDED_MAGIC_ITEM_ENGINE_HOOKS. Landing them would mark every clause naming them as owned, including untyped ones. Instead, have the compiler remove the activation-economy hook from a clause's missingHooks ONLY when that clause's operation or transition now carries a typed cost that the runtime spends (step 2). It stays on every untyped clause. Payload 'effects' clauses keep the hook unless their activation is an operation that is now typed and the clause scope is exactly that operation; document the rule you implement in the compiler code. Record the before/after counts per hook and per block, and the newly-ready / no-longer-ready delta, in your notes (use deriveItemOperationReadinessInput / assertMagicItemOperationReady as Sol did in olc5.12.11). No completeness claim follows.
4. EXCLUSIONS (record each in notes, do not implement): interItem (bag of holding / haversack / portable hole); containment (iron flask); reaction-trigger semantics beyond spending the reaction; spell casting time (already olc5.9).
PERMANENT EVIDENCE:
- An importer/curation test asserts that every typed activation cost added by this bead is backed by an exact source phrase from the vendored SRD text: the importer's evidence ledger, plus a test enumerating it. A negative sample of clauses left untyped must contain no action phrase for that operation; use a phrase regex at least as strict as the olc5.9 N3 fix.
- Runtime conformance over the REAL pack: for each newly typed state-machine transition, use_item in combat spends exactly the printed resource, refuses when it is spent, and spends nothing outside combat. Enumerate from the pack; do not hard-code. Representative newly typed operations are exercised the same way.
- Compiler readiness: a clause loses the activation hook only when its operation or transition is typed. Assert this generally over the pack.
VERIFY: run the focused importer/compiler suites, `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`, and `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing. Follow the importer-fix-protocol evidence/thaw requirements. The freeze guard is intentionally inactive until re-freeze, but write the thaw note if the protocol asks for one.
STOP and record in notes (leave the bead open) if: the source phrasing for a category is ambiguous enough that faithful typing can't be distinguished cheaply from unfaithful; the compiler cannot scope hook removal per clause without a redesign; or a decided point conflicts with code or source. Do not improvise.

TRANSITIONS: a state-machine transition has no cost field; it is driven by an operation (transitions[].via) whose typed cost use_item already spends via spendActivationTurnResource BEFORE the transition, same transaction. Plan item 2 (decided runtime) therefore needed no code change; I proved it by conformance instead. Unrecognized cost already fails closed in planItemTurnResource.

PER-CLAUSE READINESS RULE (documented in code, activationEconomyOwned): the 4 F2 hooks remain OUT of LANDED_MAGIC_ITEM_ENGINE_HOOKS; classifier drops one from missingHooks only if: operations block -> that op's typed cost is action/bonus-action/reaction; stateMachine block -> >=1 via transition and EVERY via op typed spendable; effects block -> exactly one operation references the effect, no transition does, and it is typed spendable. interItem/containment never owned. Untyped/free/consume never owned. engineHooks list untouched; other missing hooks kept.
COUNTS before->after (clauses missing hook, by hook|block): activation action economy|operations 72->29; |stateMachine 17->6; action-economy activation|effects 144->35; reaction and action economy|effects 7->4; item activation and action-budget ownership interItem 3->3, containment 1->1. Per hook: activation action economy 89->35, action-economy activation 144->35, reaction and action economy 7->4, item activation... 4->4. 166 clauses changed (43+11+108+3 hook-removals+1 that turned green).
READINESS DELTA: newly ready: magic-item:staff-of-swarming-insects/c2-effect-create-insect-cloud-payload (engine-pending->green; the hook was its only blocker). No-longer-ready: none. Green clauses 226->227, engine-pending 790->789, total 1377. Ready operations (assertMagicItemOperationReady READY list) unchanged at 19. Almost every other clause also carries other unlanded hooks (as predicted). No completeness claim.
EXCLUSIONS (recorded, not implemented): interItem (bag of holding/haversack/portable hole) 3 clauses; containment (iron flask) 1; reaction-trigger semantics beyond spending the reaction; spell casting time (olc5.9); consume/drink (above); Apparatus levers and Candle of Invocation lighting (ambiguous, follow-up bead filed).
TESTS added: test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemActivationEconomy.test.ts (12: ledger exactness vs strict phrase regex ACTION_TYPE_PHRASE, negative sample, counterfactuals, synthetic classifier rule per block, hooks not landed, independent whole-pack re-derivation of the removal rule); test/itemTransitionTurnResource.test.ts (37: enumerates every state-machine via op from the real pack; for each typed one: in combat spends exactly that resource and transitions, refuses when spent leaving state/budget untouched, spends nothing out of combat; untyped/consume spend nothing; unknown cost fails closed).
